title: Greedy
body:
# Greedy

Use greedy when a locally best decision can be shown never to hurt an optimal future answer. The proof usually comes from an exchange argument, a “stay ahead” invariant, or sorting so the decision that ends earliest/starts best dominates alternatives.

## Recognition and choices

| Goal | Usual greedy choice |
| --- | --- |
| maximum non-overlapping intervals | keep the earliest finishing interval |
| minimum jumps / coverage | extend farthest reachable boundary |
| assign resources / cookies | satisfy the smallest feasible demand first |
| remove digits / build smallest result | discard a worse earlier choice while allowed |
| buy/sell once | keep best prior minimum |

```python
def can_jump(nums: list[int]) -> bool:
    farthest = 0
    for i, jump in enumerate(nums):
        if i > farthest:
            return False
        farthest = max(farthest, i + jump)
    return True

def max_non_overlapping(intervals: list[list[int]]) -> int:
    intervals.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
    count, end = 0, float("-inf")
    for start, finish in intervals:
        if start >= end:
            count += 1
            end = finish
    return count
```

For minimum jumps, process the current reachable layer and commit a jump only when reaching its end. If a choice has a future tradeoff you cannot prove away, use [[Dynamic Programming]] or a heap instead. Be precise about whether touching intervals conflict.
